text: Sign names are chosen by the person, usually with input from parents or a sign language guide, and they can be changed by mutual agreement, which makes them different from printed names. They are not assigned to you by strangers. Often they reference something recognizable about a person, their appearance, habits, or role. For example, a person with red hair might get a name based on that, but it is not just the colour; the sign has its own place, movement, and character. In Deaf communities, a name may also point to a job, a nickname, or a shared memory. Because they are community-specific, two Deaf people may use different sign names for the same person. You cannot simply guess someone's name from their hearing name; it has to be introduced. If someone has no sign name yet, that is normal; it can be decided when they join a Deaf community.
